subject.title: [Bug]: Origin validation fails for custom URL schemes (tauri://, electron://)

question: Which open exact custom-scheme origin fix should maintainers advance for this Gateway origin-authorization bug, and what proof is sufficient for the security boundary?
rationale: Two open PRs target the same authorization helper, and the fix changes browser-origin security behavior even though the issue itself is a valid bug.

options.title: Advance one exact-origin PR
options.body: Pick the cleaner current-main candidate, require or override real behavior proof for the auth boundary, and close sibling attempts after merge.

options.title: Pause for broader origin policy
options.body: Defer the exact custom-scheme bug until maintainers decide wildcard or pattern policy, leaving affected users on the wildcard workaround longer.

options.title: Reject custom-scheme exact origins
options.body: Document wildcard or native-hosting alternatives instead, accepting the security and usability tradeoff for desktop wrappers.

recommendation.title: Advance one exact-origin PR
recommendation.body: Pick the cleaner current-main candidate, require or override real behavior proof for the auth boundary, and close sibling attempts after merge.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the Gateway origin-check surface and is the strongest history-backed routing candidate for this security-boundary choice.
